writeup.headline: Brookdale rates Strong Sell on falling revenue, heavy debt and weak share-price trend despite occupancy gains.
writeup.thesis: Brookdale scores 25, a Strong Sell, held down mainly by growth, balance sheet and valuation. Growth scores 10, with a latest-quarter revenue decline of 11.6% year on year, a TTM revenue decline of 4.4%, and growth slowed by 5.6 pp from the previous quarter. The balance sheet scores just 4: net debt is 163.64 times free cash flow and cash covers only 0.09 of debt. Valuation scores 17. P/S of 0.8x is low in absolute terms, but P/FCF of 100.5x and EV/EBIT of 59.1x are high in absolute terms, with an FCF yield 4.0 pp below the 10-year Treasury yield. Against its own history the stock is expensive (P/FCF and EV/EBIT not comparable), with P/S more expensive than at 49 of the last 61 month-ends. Trend scores 21, with the price 25.2% below its 200-day average and 40.5% below its 52-week high. The one bright spot is news: Q3 weighted average occupancy rose to 83.1%, up 130bp year over year.
key_risks: Very high leverage: net debt at 163.64 times free cash flow, with cash covering only 0.09 of debt
Thin profitability: operating margin of 3.5% and FCF margin of 0.8% leave little cushion
Revenue shrinking, with a latest-quarter revenue decline of 11.6% year on year
Diluted share count up 3.9% year on year
Weak price action: shares 38.2 pp behind SPY over the last 126 trading days
what_would_change: A 5-point rise in the composite score to 30 would lift the rating to Sell, for example through a return to revenue growth in the Q3 results due November 6
Continued occupancy gains turning into higher free cash flow would improve the quality, balance sheet and valuation scores
Debt reduction that meaningfully lowers net debt to FCF would lift the 4 balance sheet score
Strong Sell is the lowest band, but further revenue declines or a guidance cut would push the score deeper into it
